subject: Follow-up: Marketplace private offer & unit-price assumptions
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 17:02:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Marketplace private offer & unit-price assumptions

Hi Elena — great to meet earlier today. Quick recap and a couple of asks so procurement has what it needs to evaluate a marketplace private offer (AWS preferred per the call).

Recap (from our discovery):
- Estimated steady-state monthly tokens: 80M - 150M tokens/month (peak bursts up to ~250M).
- Current integration timeline: POC in May, production pilot in June, GA in Q3.
- Sensitive PHI-adjacent workloads; will need Private (VPC) option and SOC2 evidence.

Pricing inputs we discussed / need confirmed:
1) Target unit price (your desired $ per 1M tokens) — you mentioned a target range on the call; can you confirm the exact target or preferred band?
2) Expected committed spend window (monthly commit, 6/12/24 mo) — marketplace private offers require a mapping to a SKU/unit price so we can estimate discounts.
3) Procurement contact & PO cadence — please confirm who will approve private offer and if DocuSign or vendor portal is preferred.

What Redwood can provide for AWS Marketplace PO mapping:
- We can publish a private offer SKU mapped to a $/1M tokens unit price.
- We support tiered unit pricing (e.g., $X per 1M up to 100M, $Y thereafter) and/or multi-month commit mapping.
- For token-count billing we provide monthly usage reports and a Hallmark ledger export that procurement can ingest.

Action items / ask:
- Elena: please confirm the target $/1M token you want us to model (range is fine) and preferred commit term.
- Carlos (procurement): if you’re looping in procurement, can you confirm PO approver and preferred PO template?
- Redwood: we’ll draft an initial unit-price mapping spreadsheet and a PO sample for AWS private offers (attached: unit-price-proposal.xlsx).

I attached a unit-price sketch showing three mapping options: conservative, balanced, and upfront-commit (numbers are illustrative until you confirm the target band).

Available this week for a 30-min pricing alignment with procurement & partner ops: Thu 3/11 10:00–12:00 PT or Fri 3/12 09:00–11:00 PT. What works best?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales – Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0197

Attachment: unit-price-proposal.xlsx (spreadsheet, 48KB)

From: Elena Soto <elena@nimbushealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Mendez <carlos.m@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 20:18:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Marketplace private offer & unit-price assumptions

Hi Ben — thanks for the clear recap and for the attachment. I’m looping Carlos from procurement to confirm the PO workflow. A few answers below: 

- Target unit price: our internal target band for negotiations is $980 – $1,150 per 1M tokens (we would prefer to see pricing modeled at $1,000 / 1M tokens to start).
- Commit term: we’re open to a 12-month commit if the unit economics hold; will consider a 6-month pilot with a conversion to 12 months at production.
- Monthly forecast: planning estimate is 90M steady-state tokens/month after pilot (ramp from ~40M in pilot).
- Marketplace preference: AWS Private Offer is preferred (we have existing vendor workflow there).

Procurement notes (Carlos): we use a standard PO + DocuSign flow. Will need SOC2 and data-retention language up front. I’ve attached the procurement stub in the next email.

Happy to take Thu 3/11 10:30 PT for a quick alignment call.

Thanks,
Elena Soto
Head of Product, Nimbus Health
elena@nimbushealth.com | +1 617-555-8240

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 08:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Marketplace private offer & unit-price assumptions

Elena — perfect, thanks for the specifics. Quick follow-up on how we’d map that out for an AWS private offer and suggested next steps: 

1) Mapping approach (what Redwood will share in the PO):
   - Base SKU = $/1M tokens line item; we’ll model at $1,000 / 1M for the initial PO per your ask.
   - Tiering example: $1,050 / 1M up to 50M, $1,000 / 1M for 50–200M, $920 / 1M >200M (can be customized).
   - Commit overlay: a 12-month commit allows an additional 5–10% discount on the modeled unit price; we’ll show scenarios in the spreadsheet.

2) Compliance & procurement docs:
   - We will attach SOC2 Type II summary, data-residency notes, and the product security questionnaire answers to the PO package. Evelyn will lead that pack.

3) Pricing impact on Nimbus spend (ballpark):
   - At 90M steady-state tokens at $1,000 / 1M => $90k / month (billed via AWS PO pricing mapping).
   - If you commit 12 months at that average, Redwood can model to $950 / 1M effective via a commit credit structure (we’ll show the math).

Action items: I’ll update the spreadsheet with a $1,000 baseline and a 12-month commit scenario and re-share before our call. Evelyn — can you add SOC2 summary and the security questionnaire link to the packet?

See you Thu 3/11 10:30 PT — I’ll send a calendar invite to confirm.

—Ben
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
Attachment: unit-price-proposal.xlsx (updated)
